newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ long bond yields squeezed lower at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ long bond yields squeezed lower at close.

text.p: New Zealand yields surrendered most morning gains by Tuesday's close but long bond yields closed five points lower as shorts were squeezed.
All eyes are on the FOMC meeting on Wednesday morning (NZ time) where traders have factored in a 25 basis point rise in official U.S. rates.
Dealers said there was demand for the currently unfashionable long bonds as shorts were squeezed in an illiquid market.
Some traders have perceived greater value in the shorter end of the curve but were forced to turn their attention to the long end as it moved and the curve flattened.

There are mixed views about how the U.S. market will react to the expected quarter point official rate hike. Some think the market would rally on such a limited move while others see any rally as short-lived and are apprehesive about what Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan will have to say.
The short end of the market remained wary despite continued strength in the currency.
The market is still dubious about the sustainability of the New Zealand dollar's strength and about ongoing inflationary pressures.
In the event the market drifted and in the absence of direction preferred to edge higher.
The weekly T-bill tender went off uneventfully with only mild interest in the one year bills.
